close_reason: TrustAnchor struct doc now explains #[non_exhaustive] and construction guidance
description: Adding #[non_exhaustive] to TrustAnchor is a breaking change for any external caller who was constructing it with a struct literal (TrustAnchor { subject, subject_public_key_info }). No internal callers use struct literals — all use from_cert or new — but any downstream user doing so will get a compile error. The change is correct for forward compatibility but must be flagged as semver-breaking if the crate was previously published without #[non_exhaustive].
title: #[non_exhaustive] on TrustAnchor breaks struct-literal construction
